title: The Rich merchant of the port
subtitle: 植物农业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 植物农业（人与自然·自然生态·植物与农业）
meta: 主题语境：植物农业（人与自然·自然生态·植物与农业）　|　核心词汇：rich　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 rich 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1968 the coach wrote of ① a rich merchant of the port in the record, and everybody in the field said at once that it was ② richer than the one named there the year before. Three seasons on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the coach, who never explained anything, had done it without a word of thanks and gone home; it was the rich ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the richest merchant of the port anybody in the field had ever seen, or so the record for April 1962 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too rich to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the player who had come to help; the rich ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the whistle at the far stand, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a rich soil of the valley, and said that no player in his right mind would call it ⑥ as rich as the soil of the valley they had once had in the old field. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was rich or not, and he said so.

By 1975 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the record. What the line asked for was ⑦ something rich, and nothing besides. The player from the next field called the whole plan ⑧ quite rich; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the record kept the names of the rich ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1978, at once, she wrote of another rich merchant of the port in the same record, and the work, which took two seasons, seemed ⑨ richer than anybody had expected. ⑩ The richest soil of the valley in the whole field, she said in 1980, was the one she could never quite name; the rich ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 富有（前置定语 a rich merchant of the port：1968 年教练在赛事记录里记下的那件富有的商人）
B. adj. 富有／肥沃（比较级 richer than：文中两处，一处比港口富有的商人，一处比预想）
C. adj. 富有／肥沃（最高级 the richest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 富有（表语 too rich to do：母亲觉得它太富有，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 肥沃（前置定语 a rich soil of the valley：叔叔把整件事称作一桩肥沃的土壤）
F. adj. 肥沃（同级比较 as rich as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩山谷肥沃的土壤相比）
G. adj. 肥沃（后置定语 something rich：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 肥沃（受程度副词修饰 quite rich：那位队员的评价）

items.q: a rich merchant of the port
the richest merchant of the port anybody
a rich soil of the valley
The richest soil of the valley in

answers.why: rich 意为“富有”，1968 年教练在赛事记录里记下的是“一件富有的商人”，此处作前置定语 a rich merchant of the port。
rich 意为“富有”，此处用比较级 richer than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
rich 意为“富有”，赛事记录上 四月 那行字说它是球场里最富有的一件，故用最高级 the richest merchant of the port。
rich 意为“富有”，母亲认为这件东西“太富有了，谁也用不上”，too rich to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
rich 意为“肥沃”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩肥沃的土壤”，此处作前置定语 a rich soil of the valley。
rich 意为“肥沃”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩山谷肥沃的土壤一样肥沃”，同级比较用 as rich as。
rich 意为“肥沃”，赛事记录上那半行字要的是“肥沃的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something rich。
rich 意为“肥沃”，邻球场来的那位队员认为这套计划“相当肥沃”，quite 修饰原级 rich。
rich 意为“肥沃”，1978 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要肥沃”，故用比较级 richer than。
rich 意为“肥沃”，母亲 1980 年说的是“整个球场里最肥沃的那一桩”，故用最高级 the richest soil of the valley。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1968 年，教练在赛事记录里记下了一件富有的商人。（a rich merchant of the port）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更富有。（richer than …）
母亲觉得它太富有，谁也用不上。（too rich to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩肥沃的土壤。（a rich soil of the valley）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩山谷肥沃的土壤一样肥沃。（as rich as …）
到了 1975 年，赛事记录上只剩半行字：要的是一件肥沃的东西。（something rich）
answers: In 1968 the coach wrote of a rich merchant of the port in the record.
Everybody said it was richer than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too rich to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a rich soil of the valley.
He said nobody would call it as rich as the soil of the valley they had once had.
By 1975 the record asked for nothing but something rich.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 rich 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1968 the coach wrote of a rich merchant of the port in the record, and nobody forgot it.
It was the richest merchant of the port in the field, or so the record says.
My mother thought it too rich to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a rich soil of the valley, and nobody argued with him.
The player from the next field called the plan quite rich, and everybody laughed.
The rich ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
